course.title: Academic Language, Research & College Communication
course.credential_boundary: Course completion contributes 3 internal Khaemenes learning units; these are not institutional college credits.

modules.title: Academic Language, Claims & Evidence
modules.essential: How academic language makes claims precise, testable and appropriately qualified.

lessons.title: Observation, Inference & Claim
lessons.focus: Distinguish what is directly observed from what is inferred and claimed.

lessons.title: Corroboration & Context
lessons.focus: Use independent evidence and context to strengthen or limit a claim.

lessons.title: Qualification, Nuance & Scope
lessons.focus: Write claims that accurately match the strength and limits of available evidence.

modules.title: Morphology, Word Families & Disciplinary Vocabulary
modules.essential: How roots, affixes and word families support independent academic vocabulary growth.

lessons.title: Roots, Prefixes & Suffixes
lessons.focus: Analyze meaningful word parts and use morphology to infer unfamiliar academic terms.

lessons.title: Derivation & Word Families
lessons.focus: Track how grammatical form and meaning change across related words.

lessons.title: Polysemy Across Disciplines
lessons.focus: Compare how one word can carry related but distinct meanings in different fields.

modules.title: Register, Audience & Academic Voice
modules.essential: How writers adapt language to audience, purpose and disciplinary expectations.

lessons.title: Formal and Informal Register
lessons.focus: Recognize register and revise language for scholarly contexts.

lessons.title: Audience, Purpose & Tone
lessons.focus: Align vocabulary, explanation and tone with a defined audience and purpose.

lessons.title: Precision Without Pretension
lessons.focus: Prefer clear, specific language over unnecessary complexity or vague abstraction.

modules.title: Reading for Structure & Meaning
modules.essential: How skilled readers identify argument, organization, key terms and implied reasoning.

lessons.title: Close Reading & Annotation
lessons.focus: Annotate key claims, terms, evidence, definitions and questions in a source.

lessons.title: Paragraph Logic & Signposting
lessons.focus: Identify how paragraphs develop and connect ideas.

lessons.title: Summary Versus Analysis
lessons.focus: Separate faithful summary from interpretation, evaluation and response.

modules.title: Source Literacy & Credibility
modules.essential: How researchers evaluate who produced a source, why, when and with what evidence.

lessons.title: Primary, Secondary & Tertiary Sources
lessons.focus: Classify source types and choose them for appropriate research purposes.

lessons.title: Authority, Expertise & Context
lessons.focus: Evaluate source authority without treating credentials as automatic proof.

lessons.title: Bias, Perspective & Reliability
lessons.focus: Analyze perspective, incentives, omissions and evidentiary reliability.

modules.title: Research Questions & Search Strategy
modules.essential: How a broad topic becomes a focused, answerable research question.

lessons.title: From Topic to Research Question
lessons.focus: Narrow a subject into a question with manageable scope and clear concepts.

lessons.title: Keywords, Synonyms & Search Logic
lessons.focus: Build search vocabulary using related terms, controlled phrases and Boolean logic.

lessons.title: Research Trail & Search Revision
lessons.focus: Document searches, revise terms and explain why sources were kept or rejected.

modules.title: Notes, Paraphrase & Citation
modules.essential: How researchers preserve source meaning while distinguishing their own ideas.

lessons.title: Quotation, Paraphrase & Summary
lessons.focus: Choose among quotation, paraphrase and summary based on purpose.

lessons.title: Avoiding Patchwriting & Misrepresentation
lessons.focus: Paraphrase conceptually rather than replacing isolated words.

lessons.title: Citation as Evidence Trail
lessons.focus: Use citations to let a reader locate, verify and contextualize evidence.

modules.title: Argument, Counterargument & Reasoning
modules.essential: How academic writing develops a defensible position through reasons and evidence.

lessons.title: Claims, Reasons & Evidence
lessons.focus: Construct a basic argument and test whether evidence actually supports the claim.

lessons.title: Counterargument & Objection
lessons.focus: Represent opposing reasoning fairly before responding.

lessons.title: Assumptions, Warrants & Limits
lessons.focus: Identify hidden assumptions connecting evidence to conclusions.

modules.title: Synthesis Across Sources
modules.essential: How scholarly writing combines sources into a new, evidence-based interpretation.

lessons.title: Source Conversation Mapping
lessons.focus: Group sources by agreement, disagreement, method, evidence or perspective.

lessons.title: Synthesis Paragraphs
lessons.focus: Integrate multiple sources around an idea rather than summarizing them one at a time.

lessons.title: Contradiction, Uncertainty & Open Questions
lessons.focus: Represent unresolved evidence and disagreement without forcing false consensus.

modules.title: Lexical Inquiry, Meaning & Translation
modules.essential: How academic terms change across time, communities, languages and disciplines.

lessons.title: Corpus & Usage Evidence
lessons.focus: Use a defined collection of texts to examine patterns of usage.

lessons.title: Semantic Shift & Historical Meaning
lessons.focus: Trace how a term changes meaning across periods or communities.

lessons.title: Cognates, Translation & False Equivalence
lessons.focus: Compare related terms across languages while avoiding simplistic equivalence.

modules.title: Research Writing & Revision
modules.essential: How drafts develop through structure, evidence, revision and editing.

lessons.title: Thesis, Structure & Research Brief
lessons.focus: Build a defensible thesis and organize evidence around the research purpose.

lessons.title: Revision for Reasoning
lessons.focus: Revise argument structure, evidence use and paragraph logic before sentence-level editing.

lessons.title: Editing for Clarity, Style & Integrity
lessons.focus: Edit grammar, diction, citation and formatting without changing evidentiary meaning.

modules.title: Scholarly Communication & Capstone
modules.essential: How researchers present, defend and reflect on their work for different audiences.

lessons.title: Annotated Bibliography & Source Portfolio
lessons.focus: Document source relevance, credibility, method and limitations.

lessons.title: Research Presentation & Oral Defense
lessons.focus: Explain choices, evidence and limitations in a concise scholarly presentation.

lessons.title: Capstone Synthesis & Reflection
lessons.focus: Produce a final research brief and explain how the research process changed the original claim.

assessment.capstone: annotated source portfolio + synthesis research brief + presentation/defense
